newsitem.title: GERMANY: German December orders drop raises recovery doubt.
newsitem.headline: German December orders drop raises recovery doubt.

text.p: German industrial orders fell a seasonally-adjusted 1.4 percent in December following a 0.5 percent downward revision for November, new evidence of a still sluggish economy, the economics ministry said on Wednesday.

The report showed west German industrial orders fell 1.4 percent in December and offset a 0.2 percent rise in east German orders. Total domestic orders fell 0.4 percent in December while foreign orders slumped 2.7 percent.
Economists said the decline signalled the German economy was still struggling to maintain momentum after gains in industrial orders in the second and third quarters of 1996.

"The numbers, which were much worse than expected, show the economy is still in a very weak state," said Eckhard Schulte, economist at IBJ Bank in Frankfurt. "This indicates the upswing, which everyone is expecting sometime this year, may actually be pushed out further."
The fall contradicted Tuesday's surprise 1.4 percent rise in industrial output as well as positive outlook and confidence reports recently released by the Ifo economic institute.
"The string of data we have had recently show a very contradictory picture," said Stefan Bergheim, economist at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson in Frankfurt.
"We need to look at all the numbers. In the end they would give a neutral reading for the economy," Bergheim said.
But several economists said the report would not prompt the Bundesbank to trim interest rates at its fortnightly policy meeting on Thursday.

Germany's Trinkaus Capital Management said that in the months to come order intake and also industrial production should strengthen slightly, mainly due to a recovery in foreign demand tied to the weaker mark and improved competition by exporters.
The Bonn ministry said hardest hit were capital good orders, which fell 6.7 percent.
Consumer orders, helped by holiday buying, rose two percent, the ministry said. Orders in the two-month December/November period were unchanged compared to October/Septemeber.
Year-on-year pan-German orders rose 2.4 percent in December, but for December/November, the figure fell 0.4 percent compared to the same period in 1995.
